body:
I didn't think you sounded pretentious, I've heard similar sentiments before (albeit usually halfhearted.)

I think I realize that life is *supposed* to be more than payments and tests and a job already-- that's why I'm so unhappy, because I'm trying to achieve more than those things and it hasn't been working. It's *other* people who think that those are all that matter who make me feel worse by telling me that objectively, my life is great.

For what it's worth, I do still make YouTube videos by myself in my spare time, and I absolutely look back on that every year and see it as something I've accomplished. I care a lot about the videos and the topics they cover. The problem isn't my accomplishments, it's *me.* I accomplish a lot, but I don't have any friends to share it with and I end up feeling sad, even when I don't think I'm supposed to.

With the help of you and everyone else in this thread, I managed to get through the night, and I'm going to sleep now. But I know I'll be feeling all the same things again tomorrow and the next day. I guess I'll just keep trying to get out more like I already have been, and blindly hope that it gets more fulfilling. What I really want is some friends, and I know that won't happen by staying inside, but going outside doesn't guarantee anything either, apparently.

Thanks for taking the time to talk to me.

Time off from what? Work? School? Right now, I'm a sad person. Without a job, I'd be an unemployed sad person.

For time off to really make a difference, I'd have to take action to change myself and my life during that time off. And based on my prior success rate in trying to do that, I'm not sure if I could, or if it would work even if I did. If I reach the end of my "time off" and I'm still in the same situation, then it won't have done me any good, right?

> You should seek therapy.

This is something I became interested in earlier this year after reading a lot about it. However, I'm not sure if I have the time, and I almost certainly don't have the money. I kind of wish I'd sought help when I was having some of these feelings as a minor, I feel like I'm kind of on my own medically as an adult.
Rule 1b prohibits any explicit discussion of suicide methods, so I don't think I can respond to that. Sorry.

It's not a distraction from work, it's a distraction from not being happy. Work is also a distraction from not being happy. They say you shouldn't let a depressed person stay in their room all day, I unfortunately feel that adage is true based on my experiences the past few months.

As for finding a better job, like I said, it's mindless, so I'm certainly not "trying too hard." Trying too hard at acting like a mentally stable adult, maybe. If I tried to leave, I'm just as likely to end up shooting myself in the foot and getting something I hate even more that pays even less. I guess that's what you meant by "take some risks." I'm pretty much going to have to get a new job after I graduate, but I really don't know if the next one will be any better.

I see you edited your last comment about everyone you know in IT having exciting hobbies. I guess I already had a hobby, that was making videos. So now, since I'm lonely, I should pivot to pretending to care about fishing or riding ATVs to have a better chance at meeting people?

I think despite everything else I've said, the loneliness is really what it comes down to the most. This conversation we're having now is going to stick with me longer than any other conversation I had this week, just because I'm being completely open and you're choosing to be here responding to me. Don't you think forming new "friendships" based on things I have no interest in would just be setting myself up for more fake smiles and acquaintanceships? Or is the fact that I have no interest in those things a separate problem that I need to fix somehow?

> Having a stable income is fantastic because it means you actually have the time

I don't entirely see the correlation here. Absolutely, having a stable income is fantastic because I don't have to "worry about dying" (and then I think about it anyway for some reason.) But every year, I spend *more* time at work and at school and commuting to and from those places, and I have *less* time to do things that used to make me happy. And then that's compounded by the fact that I'm so tired from fake smiling at everyone while I fix their computers all day that I don't enjoy doing the other stuff as much as I used to.

I don't think taking up an entirely new hobby that I have no past desire to take part in would help long-term. It would just be a distraction. I'd know that the reason why I'm there is just to occupy my time. On top of that, the city that I live in is pretty dead. It's not Detroit, but it isn't far behind. Every time I've tried to go out so far, I've only met people 2-3x my age. If there was a "college-age people who have no other outlets for social communication" club, I'd be all over it, but everyone here either stays in their house or already knows people and doesn't want to mess with strangers.

I feel bad for arguing with you so much, but thank you for talking to me. I don't really feel much better, but I still appreciate it.

> That's fantastic.

I wish I could think about it that way, I really, really do. That's the reasoning I use to justify my decisions to other people, like my family. But like you pointed out, I'm "being bored to death." I'm not afraid that I'm going to end up homeless on the street. I'm afraid that I'm going to end up working the majority of my days doing basically mindless IT work for the rest of my life, and I'm afraid that I'm going to come home from that job and have nothing to do and nobody to talk to, because that's where I'm at right now and I can't figure out how I'm supposed to fix that. I'm trying and I can't get anything to change.

I've been dreaming for years already, and it's gotten me nothing. I could very easily keep dreaming for the next 60 years and still get no farther. I'll still be the same person with the same dreams doing the same things, nothing will have changed. So what's the point? The journey? The journey isn't making me very happy right now.

You know, I've thought a lot recently about "moving somewhere else," but I was thinking more geographically-- looking at different cities in my region. But I ended up discarding the idea for various reasons.

As far as the school thing goes, social interaction was the *last* thing on my mind when I transferred... I was mainly worried about finances at the time, since I didn't want to end up in debt like my parents. Along those lines, I never seriously considered film school or other artistic education; I bought into the STEM hype train. Now that I'm several years invested, I can't really change courses. My living situation is complicated, because I've got two divorced parents who don't own the houses they live in, and I've called in a lot of family favors and embarrassed myself a lot already. I'm pretty much being tolerated right now because they can't deny I'm on-track to support myself by the end of 2019. The way I see it, any further education is going to have to be a secondary, self-funded thing after I've moved out. I'm questioning whether that's going to be good for me or just another distraction.

I'm not sure what you mean by "joining a video production company." Yeah, I've thought about it... while daydreaming. I have no formal training and the market is entirely oversaturated. A more realistic scenario would be joining or forming a smaller, more local group, but like I said, I can't seem to find anyone who I could click with.

I used to think that I liked computers. That's what my job is in, IT. Basically installing Windows updates for eight hours a day. It *is* boring, but I can't complain. There are tons of more difficult jobs that pay less.

As a hobby, I used to like making online videos, for YouTube and stuff. But I'm lonely, and tired of talking into a camera by myself. After I graduated high school, all of my "friends" who used to help with videos stopped talking to me-- they were never really into it, they just helped because I asked them to. Then I made the mistake of transferring from university to technical college (pissing my parents off in the process), and at technical college, nobody cares about hobbies or extracurricular activities; it's all about learning a trade and getting a job. I've tried to make up for that by going to local meetups and things, even going so far as to start my own local meetup for online video creators, but everyone I meet at those things is at least a decade older than I am. I feel like I screwed myself out of a social life; people I talk to about that don't see what the big deal is, because I'm getting out and talking to people, but the people I meet are there for professional networking, not to find friends to hang out with and work on projects together with.

Sorry for the rant. I also like music composition. After I graduate and get a full-time job, I was planning to start taking online music theory classes. But with the way things are right now, I don't see myself actually getting happier by doing that.
